audit_findings.title: The scenarios do not capture the binary risk of a U.S. import exclusion
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (FY2026 U.S. revenue was $1,569.0m; revenue attributable to affected products is not filed)
audit_findings.mechanism: An exclusion could reduce owner earnings and growth through lost U.S. sales, redesign costs, inventory losses, and legal costs.
audit_findings.evidence: An adverse ruling at the ITC could result in an order excluding certain of our products from the U.S. market, which would have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an active proceeding rather than a generic risk, and the company states that an adverse ITC ruling could have a material adverse effect. Every scenario preserves the $683.6m anchor, so even the bear case omits the possible step-down. The record does not establish the probability or affected revenue, but the remedy is reasonably capable of materially changing operating value.
audit_findings.action: Map the accused products to FY2026 U.S. revenue and gross profit, obtain the ITC schedule and remedy assessment, evaluate design-around timing and cost, and rerun probability-weighted exclusion and redesign cases.

audit_findings.title: Adding all $611.2 million of cash and investments may overstate distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $611.199m bridge amount; $1,532.6m purchase commitments; complete removal would reduce value by $10.085 per share, or 5.98% of base value, from $168.57 to $158.49
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for procurement, cancellation claims, or minimum operating liquidity is not excess and should be withheld from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026 we had $ 1,532.6 million of purchase commitments with these third parties.
audit_findings.explanation: The purchase commitments are not themselves demonstrated debt or an immediate $1,532.6m liability, and the filing reports no significant recorded cancellation liabilities. Nevertheless, the bridge treats all cash as distributable without establishing required liquidity. The maximum bridge classification at issue is large enough to affect the valuation, but the record cannot determine the proper adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain commitment payment schedules and cancellation terms, identify components already purchased by manufacturers, forecast inventory conversion and operating cash needs, determine minimum liquidity, and rerun the bridge using only verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Inventory reserves could be understating the anchor's economic costs
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (finished goods were $703.361m, total inventory $780.440m, and FY2026 excess-and-obsolete provision $4.104m)
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional write-downs would reduce operating owner earnings and could lower the normalized anchor if obsolescence is recurring.
audit_findings.evidence: We identified the assessment of the valuation of certain excess or obsolete finished goods inventory as a critical audit matter.
audit_findings.explanation: The critical audit matter demonstrates substantial estimation uncertainty, not that the recorded reserve is wrong. Finished goods represent 90.1% of total inventory, while the filed provision was only 0.53% of total inventory, so a forecast error could be meaningful. SKU-level evidence needed to determine the loss and its recurrence is absent.
audit_findings.action: Review SKU aging, post-year-end sell-through, forecast-to-actual history, markdowns, product transitions, and reserve sensitivities; then restate historical owner earnings and rerun the anchor for any demonstrated shortfall.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require recurring working-capital investment absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 inventory and vendor deposits absorbed $138.966m; comparable net core operating working-capital outflow was $2.853m in FY2026 and $48.540m in FY2025; normalized future deduction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental receivables, inventory, vendor deposits, and other operating assets consume cash, while payables, deferred revenue, and other operating liabilities finance part of that consumption; the normalized net requirement should reduce projected owner earnings and growth cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: These mitigation efforts have caused our inventory and vendor deposit balances to increase in the past, and they may cause such increases in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed cash flows demonstrate substantial gross investment in inventory and vendor deposits, but FY2026 supplier financing offset most core working-capital uses. The supplied valuation does not demonstrate a normalized working-capital deduction, yet two years are insufficient to establish the recurring amount or whether the FY2026 payable increase is sustainable. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct five-to-ten-year operating working capital by component, separate timing effects from growth requirements, test the sustainability of supplier financing, and rerun each scenario with sales-linked normalized incremental working capital.

audit_findings.title: A material IRS claim is unreserved and absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $50.0m excluding interest and penalties; $0.825 per share and 0.49% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse judgment would create a claim ahead of common equity and reduce the equity bridge; associated defense costs could also reduce owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates the incremental tax liability associated with the income adjustment proposed in the AOF would be approximately $ 50.0 million, excluding potential interest and penalties, after adjusting for the impact of an adjustment on the amount of transition tax paid and payable in future years by the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential liability is real and unreserved, but a full deduction of the filed $50.0m would reduce base value only from $168.57 to approximately $167.74 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. Interest and penalties are unquantified, so they should still be updated, but the quantified principal is not material to the DCF.
audit_findings.action: Update the Tax Court status, obtain a filed or counsel-supported estimate of interest and penalties, confirm no duplication with recorded tax liabilities, and deduct the probability-weighted total in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Uncapped indemnification exposure is not recognized in the valuation
audit_findings.mechanism: Triggered indemnification payments, defense costs, settlements, or customer reimbursements would reduce owner earnings or create a liability deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required to make under these indemnification agreements is not estimable and the Company has not incurred any material costs to defend lawsuits or settle claims related to these indemnification agreements to date.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual maximum is unlimited, but the filing reports no material historical defense or settlement costs, no recorded liability, and a minimal estimated fair value. No supplied evidence shows that a material indemnification demand has been made. Active patent disputes make this a forward-looking exposure requiring monitoring rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Check whether the AX Wireless, Velocity, or Intellectual Ventures matters have generated customer notices or indemnification demands; review affected agreements, insurance, supplier recoveries, and accrual assessments, and rerun only when a probable or probability-weighted exposure can be supported.
